metadata.baselayout_description: {{projects.skill-recommendation-engine.metrics.recommendationRelevance}} recommendation relevance. Sub-50ms inference on a single NVIDIA T4. Weighted directed graph over multi-level skill hierarchies with dynamic node updates.

blocks.graph_based_skill_recommendation_engine_: {{projects.skill-recommendation-engine.metrics.recommendationRelevance}} relevance, sub-50ms inference. Weighted directed graph over multi-level skill hierarchies - dynamic node updates without batch retraining, deterministic traversal under production load.
blocks.the_problem_th_body: The recommendation system treated related skills as independent nodes with no structural modeling - hierarchical relationships were ignored entirely. Every taxonomy expansion triggered full batch retraining, blocking updates until recompute completed. Inference latency under production concurrency exceeded the sub-50ms SLA required for live platform use.
blocks.the_system_th_body_2: encoding multi-level skill hierarchy relationships as typed edges with dynamic weight updates. Lightweight mathematical scoring heuristics minimize computational overhead per inference call - no neural inference at query time. The update model handles dynamic node additions without full graph recomputation: adding a new skill inserts a node and its edges; existing traversal paths are unaffected.
blocks.the_system_th_body_3: Deterministic traversal logic produces consistent outputs under frequent profile and taxonomy updates. The graph structure constrains traversal depth, so worst-case latency is knowable before deployment. Latency profiled at the
blocks.the_system_th_body_4: under realistic concurrency during testing on NVIDIA T4 - not average latency under ideal conditions.
blocks.outcomes_th_body_2: on a single NVIDIA T4 under full test load - 99th percentile SLA met. Dynamic taxonomy expansion no longer triggers batch retraining. Consistent outputs maintained under frequent profile and taxonomy changes.
